assertions.description: Keyboard.prototype.lock is a function. This is the API behind ClientSideDetectionType KEYBOARD_LOCK_REQUESTED, the scam-check trigger Google names. Only the API's presence is checked, not the scan.
Element.prototype.requestFullscreen is a function (trigger type FULLSCREEN_API).
Element.prototype.requestPointerLock is a function (trigger type POINTER_LOCK_REQUESTED).
document.fullscreenEnabled is true for this top-level document, so a gesture-started fullscreen session is allowed by policy. The legitimate-patterns concept depends on this.
Without a user gesture, requestFullscreen() rejects, so a page cannot silently grab or re-enter fullscreen.
assertions.test: Running this automatically would itself request fullscreen (a FULLSCREEN_API trigger) on every visit. Exercise it with the 'try to re-enter fullscreen automatically' option at /v155/server-side-gemini-powered-scam-checks-for-desktop/legitimate-fullscreen-patterns/: the log shows the browser's rejection.

assertions.description: On desktop, page text is sent to the server-side Gemini model only for Enhanced Safe Browsing users, and only after a page shows high-confidence scam indicators. The text is processed ephemerally.
assertions.test: Browser-internal Safe Browsing behaviour with no web-exposed surface. Pages cannot observe scans or verdicts. Observe client-side detection activity manually in chrome://safe-browsing with Enhanced Protection enabled.

assertions.description: SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel = 2 (EnhancedProtection) enrolls managed profiles. 1 and 0 exclude them from the server-side check.
assertions.test: Needs a managed browser. Deploy the artifact from the enrollment-and-policy concept and confirm it in chrome://policy and chrome://settings/security.
